verses.verse:
जलाभिषाली क्वचिदल्प भूमौ दीर्घेण धैर्येण खनन् यथा हि।
उपैत्यगाधम् सलिलं तथैव कालेन साध्यः खलु राग एकः।१४७।
verses.text: Just as one who longs for water, digging with long patience in one small piece of ground, reaches deep water, in the same way one rāga is indeed to be mastered over time.

commentary.text: That is, just as a person who wants to find water does not dig a little in many places but digs patiently and long at one single point and reaches deep water, in the same way it is necessary for practitioners (sādhakas) to ripen one single rāga patiently over a long time, and then to transfer whatever mastery (siddhi) has been gained in that rāga to other rāgas, one by one. For a rāga is only a means; what is to be achieved is svara (note) and tāla themselves. If the arrangement of notes is mastered in one rāga, then arrangement of the same level is possible in other rāgas too. Those who learn a different rāga every day gain nothing even after years. Well-wishing gurus give their dear disciple training (tālīm) in one single rāga for two or three years. Therefore in this book too, gats and so on are being written through just one or two rāgas. For other rāgas it will be necessary to consult other books.
